query_text: What medicine should I take when I get a cold?

message.content:
Based on information from medical authorities, here is guidance on what to take when you have a cold:

## Important Facts First

- **There is no cure for the common cold.** Most colds improve on their own within 7–10 days.
- **Antibiotics do not work** against cold viruses and should not be used.
- **Rest and hydration** are the most important treatments.

## Over-the-Counter (OTC) Medications by Symptom

| Symptom | Recommended Medication | Notes |
|---------|----------------------|-------|
| **Fever, headache, sore throat, body aches** | Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or Ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) | Follow label directions; don't exceed recommended doses |
| **Nasal congestion/stuffy nose** | Decongestants with **pseudoephedrine** (Sudafed) | Oral phenylephrine was found ineffective by the FDA in 2024; nasal sprays work but don't use >3–5 days |
| **Runny nose** | Antihistamines (limited benefit for colds) | May help when combined with decongestants; first-generation types cause drowsiness |
| **Cough** | Dextromethorphan (for severe cough only) | Honey works for adults and children >1 year; most coughs don't need suppression |

## Non-Drug Remedies

- **Saline nasal spray or rinses** to clear mucus
- **Humidifier or cool-mist vaporizer** to moisten air
- **Warm liquids** (chicken soup, tea with honey, warm water with lemon)
- **Saltwater gargle** for sore throat
- **Throat lozenges** (not for children under 4)

## Important Warnings

- **Children under 6:** Avoid OTC cough/cold medicines; use only acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever (with correct dosing)
- **Never give aspirin to children or teenagers** (risk of Reye's syndrome)
- **Never give honey to infants under 1 year** (risk of botulism)
- **Avoid zinc nasal sprays** (risk of permanent loss of smell)
- **Check combination products** to avoid duplicating ingredients, especially acetaminophen (liver risk)
- **Consult your doctor** before using decongestants if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, thyroid problems, or prostate issues

## When to See a Doctor

- Trouble breathing or fast breathing
- Fever lasting more than 4 days
- Symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement
- Symptoms that improve then worsen
- Severe dehydration

If you're unsure which medications are safe for you, consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist, especially if you take prescription medications or have chronic health conditions.

---

Sources:
1. https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/treatment/index.html
2. https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/common-cold/diagnosis-treatment/drc-20351611
3. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/decongestants-antihistamines-cold
4. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/otc-cold-medicines
5. https://www.webmd.com/cold-and-flu/understanding-common-cold-treatment
